newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper firmer after Escondida strike news.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper firmer after Escondida strike news.

text.p: COMEX copper moved higher in early trading following news of a strike at Escondida mine in Chile, but there was no sign yet of any frantic buying and early gains were soon pared after the initial pop, traders said.
Escondida is the world's biggest copper mine, producing over 800,000 tonnes annually.
Some 120 miners, less than 20 percent of the workforce, have gone on strike as of the first shift Friday, with another 80 expected to join this evening.
A small union at the mine voted earlier this week to strike.
"I don't see any big panic buying - strikes in that part of the world are pretty commonplace and they rarely last a long time," Lawson Spence of Smith Barney said.

However, he noted that LME stocks continue to drift downward making the nearby situation very tight. If LME three months closes above the key $2,300 per tonne chart area, some more follow-through buying could come in to spur a rally.
LME reported Friday that stocks fell 1,350 tonnes to 152,475 tonnes.
At 0920 EDT May COMEX copper was up 1.30 cents at 106.80 cents per pound, traded 107.50 to 106.00 cents. Spot April was up 1.75 cents at 108.00 cents.
